items.name: a unique with a record and two sockets
an ethereal class item with an automagic term
a large value at a capped buyer

text.intro: Type a toy item and a toy buyer; the table walks the buy and the sell value step by step. The numbers offered first are illustrative.

caps.grade: Quality: 1 low, 2 normal, 5 set, 7 unique (any other number reads as normal)
caps.recMult: Set or unique record: cost multiplier
caps.recAdd: Set or unique record: cost add
caps.auto: Has an automagic affix: yes (1) or no (0)
caps.kind: Class item (own type class below 7): yes (1) or no (0)
caps.sell: Buyer: sell multiplier (price paid by the player)
caps.buy: Buyer: buy multiplier (value paid to the player)
caps.reduce: Reduced prices of the player, 0 to 99

steps.terms: Terms of the automagic affix and the quality

calc.terms: each term is (m x value) / 1024 + a, divided first when the buy value is above 65535; a low item gets minus half of each value instead; none when not identified
calc.sockets: plus half the cost of each child
calc.value: sell value / 4 again for a class item
calc.npc: each value scaled by its multiplier over 1024, divided first above 65535
calc.ceiling: the sell value is at most the buyer's largest
calc.price: buy value less its reduction; each at least 1

text.note: Computed by our model of the price core for modes 0 and 1, not observed in the game. Left out: the repair value and mode 3, items that are armour, tomes, quivers, ears, body parts or stacks, magic, rare, crafted, superior and tempered items (the per-stat terms of C5 and the staff-mod term), a quest group of the buyer, the quantity, durability and the gamble price. Items of those kinds are not priced by this table.
